title: Acute inflammation, in focus
promise: Explain vascular changes, neutrophil recruitment and resolution using anatomically identified structures.

scenes.narration: Local injury activates resident cells. Their inflammatory mediators signal nearby vessels and recruit immune defenses.
scenes.visual: Identify a local injury above the vessel; dim the surrounding tissue.

scenes.narration: Arterioles dilate, increasing local blood flow. This contributes to the redness and warmth of acute inflammation.
scenes.visual: Focus the arteriolar inflow and widen its lumen without calling a capillary an arteriole.

scenes.narration: Increased permeability, especially in postcapillary venules, lets fluid and plasma proteins enter tissue, contributing to swelling.
scenes.visual: Identify postcapillary venule; show protein-rich fluid crossing into tissue.

scenes.narration: Neutrophils roll, adhere, and cross the venular wall. They then follow chemical signals toward the injury.
scenes.visual: Track a segmented-nucleus neutrophil through rolling, adhesion and transmigration.

scenes.narration: When the trigger is controlled, active resolution limits recruitment and clears debris. These overlapping processes are compressed here for teaching.
scenes.visual: Fade to a restrained repair state; label teaching-time compression, not a literal biological clock.
